#recipeideas #gelatin  Gelatin is collagen just in a different form. Collagen is a structural protein found in animal tissues like skin, bones, and connective tissue. When you take that collagen and cook it (heat + water), it breaks down into gelatin. What actually happens: 	•	Collagen has a tight, triple-helix structure (very strong and rigid) 	•	When heated, that structure unwinds and partially breaks down 	•	This creates a softer, more digestible form → gelatin So when you see: “Unflavored natural gelatin (bovine)” 	•	“Bovine” = comes from cows 	•	“Unflavored” = no additives 	•	“Gelatin” = collagen that has been hydrolyzed by heat

THE ONE YOU’VE ALL BEEN WAITING FOR: COLLAGEN CHAT (Girl Science Edition) 🩷 First up, collagen is important. It’s what keeps your skin bouncy, joints cushioned, and tissues strong. Your body makes collagen, but rom your mid-20s, that production starts to dip – and drops faster post-menopause thanks to hormonal changes. DO YOU NEED TO TAKE A COLLAGEN SUPPLEMENT? Collagen supplements don’t “top up” your collagen directly. They’re broken down into small peptides that signal your body to make more, but only if your body’s in the right state to respond. That generally comes from you sleeping well, eating a balanced diet with enough protein and managing your stress, Without those foundations, the signal’s weak – and your collagen powder probably won’t do much. Where collagen actually delivers: 💞Joints: Hydrolysed or type II collagen can help reduce joint pain and slow cartilage breakdown (especially if osteoarthritis runs in your family). 🌟Skin: Evidence is mixed. High-quality, independent studies show minimal benefit for elasticity or hydration. 💅Hair & nails: Not much science here yet. Takehome message: collagen can support you, but it’s not a miracle. Focus on your foundations first – balanced nutrition, sleep, and stress management – and collagen becomes the cherry on top, not the whole sundae 🍒 #collagen #collagenforwomen #girlscience #womenshealth #hormonehealth

The best collagen is one that’s hydrolysed, formulated with Type 1 & Type 3 collagen and contains. Here’s Why:   ✅Hydrolyzed Collagen Hydrolysis is a process that breaks down the large, intact collagen protein molecules into smaller peptides.  This is crucial for several reasons:  🙌🏾Faster Absorption and Digestion:  The smaller hydrolyzed peptides are easier for your body to break down in the digestive tract and absorb into the bloodstream  This allows the collagen to reach target tissues (like skin, bones, and joints) more quickly and effectively. 🙌🏾Bioavailability: Hydrolyzed collagen (collagen peptides) has high bioavailability, meaning a greater percentage of it is actually absorbed and used by the body compared to non-hydrolyzed, native collagen  🙌🏾Solubility: Hydrolyzed collagen dissolves easily in liquids, making it convenient to incorporate into drinks and food.  ✅Type 1 & Type 3 Collagen Collagen is the most abundant protein in the body, but different types serve different functions. Type 1 and Type 3 are the most common types found in the body and are often supplemented together because they work synergistically:  🙌🏾Type 1 Collagen: This is the primary component of skin, tendons, ligaments, and bone. It is responsible for skin elasticity and strength, and healthy bones. 🙌🏾Type 3 Collagen: Often found alongside Type 1, Type 3 is prevalent in muscles, arteries, and internal organs. It contributes to the structure and health of the skin and blood vessels. Synergy: Supplementing with both ensures comprehensive support for the most common collagen-dependent structures in the body, promoting faster and more visible results across a range of tissues  ✅Vitamin C Vitamin C does not just boost immunity; it is a vital co-factor in collagen synthesis within the body:  🙌🏾Essential for Synthesis: Your body cannot produce collagen without adequate Vitamin C. The vitamin is required for the hydroxylation process that stabilizes the collagen molecule during its formation. 🙌🏾Faster, More Effective Results: Including Vitamin C in the supplement ensures that once the absorbed collagen peptides reach their target areas, the body has the necessary components to actively use them to build new, stable collagen fibers [ Without it, the body's natural collagen production process would be inhibited, slowing down any potential benefits.
